Write the system as \(AX = B\):
\(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix},\ X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix},\ B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(|A| = (1)(3) - (2)(2) = 3 - 4 = -1 \neq 0\), so \(A^{-1}\) exists.

\(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\,\text{adj}(A) = \dfrac{1}{-1}\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(X = A^{-1}B = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -6+6 \\ 4-3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\).

Hence \(x = 0,\ y = 1\).

Write the system as \(AX = B\):
\(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix},\ X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix},\ B = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(|A| = (1)(-1) - (1)(2) = -1 - 2 = -3 \neq 0\), so \(A^{-1}\) exists.

\(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{-3}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(X = A^{-1}B = \dfrac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\).

Hence \(x = 3,\ y = 1\).

Write the system as \(AX = B\):
\(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix},\ X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix},\ B = \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(|A| = (2)(3) - (6)(1) = 6 - 6 = 0\).

Since \(|A| = 0\), \(A^{-1}\) does not exist, so the inversion method fails. Dividing the first equation by 2 gives \(x + 3y = 4\), while the second equation is \(x + 3y = 5\). These are contradictory, so the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

Write the system as \(AX = B\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}\).

Form \([A|B]\) and reduce:
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & -3 \end{array}\right]\).

Apply \(R_2 \to 2R_2 - 3R_1\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 7 & -21 \end{array}\right]\).

From \(R_2\): \(7y = -21 \Rightarrow y = -3\).
From \(R_1\): \(2x + y = 5 \Rightarrow 2x - 3 = 5 \Rightarrow x = 4\).

Hence \(x = 4,\ y = -3\).

Write the system as \(AX = B\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}\).

Form \([A|B]\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 5 & 4 \end{array}\right]\).

Apply \(R_2 \to R_2 - 3R_1\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & -2 \end{array}\right]\).

From \(R_2\): \(-4y = -2 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
From \(R_1\): \(x + 3y = 2 \Rightarrow x + \dfrac{3}{2} = 2 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

Hence \(x = \dfrac{1}{2},\ y = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

Write the system as \(AX = B\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}\).

Form \([A|B]\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 6 \end{array}\right]\).

Apply \(R_2 \to 3R_2 - 4R_1\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 7 & 14 \end{array}\right]\).

From \(R_2\): \(7y = 14 \Rightarrow y = 2\).
From \(R_1\): \(3x - y = 1 \Rightarrow 3x - 2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1\).

Hence \(x = 1,\ y = 2\).

Write the system as \(AX = B\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 7 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).

Form \([A|B]\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 5 & 2 & 4 \\ 7 & 3 & 5 \end{array}\right]\).

Apply \(R_2 \to 5R_2 - 7R_1\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 5 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \end{array}\right]\).

From \(R_2\): \(y = -3\).
From \(R_1\): \(5x + 2y = 4 \Rightarrow 5x - 6 = 4 \Rightarrow x = 2\).

Hence \(x = 2,\ y = -3\).

Let the cost (in Rs.) of one pencil, one pen and one eraser be \(x,\ y,\ z\) respectively. The conditions give:
\(4x + 3y + 2z = 60\)
\(2x + 4y + 6z = 90\)
\(6x + 2y + 3z = 70\)

Write as \(AX = B\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 6 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 60 \\ 90 \\ 70 \end{bmatrix}\).

Form \([A|B]\) and reduce. Apply \(R_2 \to \tfrac{1}{2}R_2\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 4 & 3 & 2 & 60 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 45 \\ 6 & 2 & 3 & 70 \end{array}\right]\).

Apply \(R_3 \to R_3 - R_2\):
\(5x = 25 \Rightarrow x = 5\).

From \(R_2\): \(x + 2y + 3z = 45 \Rightarrow 2y + 3z = 40\).
From \(R_1\): \(4x + 3y + 2z = 60 \Rightarrow 3y + 2z = 40\).

Subtracting, \((2y + 3z) - (3y + 2z) = 0 \Rightarrow z - y = 0 \Rightarrow z = y\). Then \(2y + 3y = 40 \Rightarrow 5y = 40 \Rightarrow y = 8\), and \(z = 8\).

Hence a pencil costs Rs. 5, a pen costs Rs. 8 and an eraser costs Rs. 8.

Let the three numbers be \(x,\ y,\ z\). The conditions give:
\(x + y + z = 2\)
\((x + z) - 2y = 8 \Rightarrow x - 2y + z = 8\)
\(3x + (y + z) = 4 \Rightarrow 3x + y + z = 4\)

Write as \(AX = B\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 8 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}\).

Form \([A|B]\) and reduce. Apply \(R_2 \to R_2 - R_1\) and \(R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -2 \end{array}\right]\).

From \(R_2\): \(-3y = 6 \Rightarrow y = -2\).
From \(R_3\): \(-2y - 2z = -2 \Rightarrow 4 - 2z = -2 \Rightarrow z = 3\).
From \(R_1\): \(x + y + z = 2 \Rightarrow x - 2 + 3 = 2 \Rightarrow x = 1\).

Hence the numbers are \(x = 1,\ y = -2,\ z = 3\).

Let the cost price (in Rs.) of a T.V. set be \(x\) and of a V.C.R. be \(y\).

Total cost of 3 T.V. sets and 2 V.C.R.s: \(3x + 2y = 35000\).

Selling price of a T.V. set \(= x + 1000\) and of a V.C.R. \(= y + 500\). Revenue from 2 T.V. sets and 1 V.C.R.:
\(2(x + 1000) + (y + 500) = 21500 \Rightarrow 2x + y = 19000\).

Write as \(AX = B\):
\(\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 35000 \\ 19000 \end{bmatrix}\).

Form \([A|B]\) and apply \(R_1 \to R_1 - 2R_2\):
\(\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 0 & -3000 \\ 2 & 1 & 19000 \end{array}\right]\).

From \(R_1\): \(-x = -3000 \Rightarrow x = 3000\).
From \(R_2\): \(2x + y = 19000 \Rightarrow 6000 + y = 19000 \Rightarrow y = 13000\).

Hence the cost price of a T.V. set is Rs. 3000 and of a V.C.R. is Rs. 13000. The selling prices are: T.V. set \(= 3000 + 1000 = \) Rs. 4000 and V.C.R. \(= 13000 + 500 = \) Rs. 13500.
